_source: Great Britain and Northern Ireland, the 12 game regions (nine English regions, Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland). Two types. secondary_school: Britain has no published split of teachers by upper years, so its school type is its own, not upper_secondary_school: the state-funded secondary schools (ages 11 to 18, sixth forms included), figure secondary_pupils_per_teacher = the pupils of those schools over their teachers in full-time equivalents, school year 2025/26, one release per nation, one definition: publicly funded secondary schools, pupils (full-time equivalents where the release gives them, a headcount where it does not), teachers in full-time equivalents. England (nine regions): Department for Education, School workforce in England, reporting year 2025, file workforce_ptrs_2010_2025_nat_reg_la.csv (https://explore-education-statistics.service.gov.uk/find-statistics/school-workforce-in-england/2025), rows time_period 202526, regional level, 'State-funded secondary': number_schools, pupils_fte, teachers_fte; London is published as Inner and Outer London and is added. Scotland: Scottish Government, Pupil and teacher characteristics 2025, headline statistics (https://www.gov.scot/publications/pupil-and-teacher-characteristics-2025/pages/headline-statistics/): 359 publicly funded secondary schools, 315 503 pupils (a headcount), 25 067 teachers (full-time equivalents). Wales: Welsh Government, Schools' census results: January 2026 (https://www.gov.wales/schools-census-results-january-2026-html, tables 1, 6 and 8 of its spreadsheet): 173 maintained secondary schools, 169 823.5 full-time equivalent pupils, 9 680.5 full-time equivalent qualified teachers (heads and deputies included); middle schools (pupils aged 3 to 18) are a separate sector and are not counted. Northern Ireland: Department of Education and NISRA, Annual enrolments at schools 2025/26 (https://datavis.nisra.gov.uk/DEstatistics/annual-enrolments-schools-and-funded-pre-school-education-northern-ireland-202526.html: 190 post-primary schools, 156 766 pupils, a headcount) and Teacher workforce statistics bulletin 2025/26 (https://datavis.nisra.gov.uk/DEstatistics/teacher-workforce-statistics-bulletin-202526.html: 10 321.1 full-time equivalent post-primary teachers, grammar and non-grammar schools). units = those schools, capacity = those pupils. The level of a region is its pupils over its teachers; national = the 12 regions' pupils over their teachers (16.30); the levels weighted by the regions' `share` give it back within 0.6 % (the loader's tolerance is 3 %). hospital: units = NHS provider organisations that report beds (trusts in England, boards in Scotland, five HSC trusts in Northern Ireland; the Welsh release names no count, so 0), not hospitals; capacity = average available beds, year 2024/25 except Wales 2023-24 (the later Welsh totals are not published: the Swansea Bay figures are missing). England: NHS England, KH03 Bed Availability and Occupancy Data - Overnight, NHS Trust by Sector, Q4 2024-25 (https://www.england.nhs.uk/statistics/statistical-work-areas/bed-availability-and-occupancy/bed-data-overnight/), average daily available overnight beds of 183 trusts; each trust is placed in the English region of its registered postcode (NHS ODS API, ONS regions through postcodes.io), so a trust with sites in two regions counts wholly in one (the NHS regions' totals are not reproduced exactly: about 1.3 % of the beds sit in a different region than the trust's NHS region). Scotland: Public Health Scotland, Annual NHS beds information, beds by health board and specialty, All Specialties, average available staffed beds, 2024/25 (20 234). Wales: Welsh Government, NHS beds: April 2023 to March 2024 (10 447). Northern Ireland: Department of Health, Hospital statistics: inpatient and day case activity 2024/25 (4 934.9, the four trusts of the release). The definitions differ a little by nation (available overnight beds, staffed beds, average available beds). hospital_beds_per_1000 = beds over the ONS mid-2024 population (Nomis NM_2002_1), national 2.42 over the 12 regions. The catalogue's hospital capacity (693) is the mean of the English trusts that report any general and acute beds: a trust runs several hospitals, and no table gives hospitals. Self-checks: the English trusts add up to NHS England's total (132 178), the Scottish boards to Scotland's total within rounding. Licences: Open Government Licence v3.0 for every source (DfE, NHS England, Scottish Government, Public Health Scotland, Welsh Government, DoH and DE Northern Ireland, ONS). Read 2026-11-17.
